pilot: Elevator Quest voice casting pilot, audition takes (three roles)
status: audition only; nothing chosen. The owner chooses by ear on the listening page.
note_on_listening: The agent that made these takes cannot hear. Nothing here describes how a take sounds; voices are not ranked.
pricing_observed: 1 credit per character of the text sent, per take; tags, ellipses and punctuation count. One library voice (Dexter Glitch VF) was estimated at 2.25 times that rate and was not used.

unrecoverable_runs.what: An earlier pass of this pilot ran 13 more nodes in the same flow (two takes each, default count). Their session ids were lost when that pass was cut off, so their audio could not be fetched or measured and is not on the page. The credits are counted from a no-charge estimate of those exact nodes (1,038), which matched the per-character pricing.

nodes.voice: angus (first run, separate A1/A2/A3 nodes; voice id not recovered)
jimmy (first run, C1 and C2; voice id not recovered)

plan_vs_done.planned: Elevator: 4 voices x A1+A2+A3; Lifty: 5 voices x B1, B2, B3; Crew: 3 voices x C1, C2; 2 takes each.
plan_vs_done.done: Elevator: Carolyn as three separate pieces (first pass), Samuel, Ava and Benjamin as one combined A1+A2+A3 passage. Lifty: Sheldon B1, B2, B3; Zibby, Wilf, Kai and Sigma B1 and B2. Crew: Dan C1 and C2; Kiara and Jamie C1.
dropped_for_budget: B3 for Zibby, Wilf, Kai, Sigma
the [calmly] tag on the combined announcer passage
comparability_notes: Carolyn's announcements are three separate generations with [calmly] (A1 also had a [pause] between its two phrases); the other three announcers read one passage without a tag, separated by ellipses. Judge cadence with that in mind.
Within each other piece, every voice received exactly the same text.

direction.A: Fewest tags: the voices were chosen for calm, measured delivery, so the combined passage relies on full stops and ellipses for the gaps between announcements.
direction.B1: [warmly] at the start; commas give the checklist rhythm.
direction.B2: A [pause] after the call, and a comma after 'Press 8' so the number lands before the instruction finishes. Digits kept as written.

transcript_method: Every take transcribed blind with a local faster-whisper small.en model (int8, beam 5, no prompt). Number words and digits are treated as equal; 'Liftee' and similar spellings of the invented name are accepted as a transcriber spelling, not as a misreading.
measurement_method: ffprobe duration; ffmpeg loudnorm (integrated loudness, true peak); ffmpeg silencedetect at -40 dB, 0.12 s for pauses. Words per second = expected word count / file duration.

listening_page.path_outside_repo: scratchpad casting-eq/elevator-quest-voice-casting.html (not committed; audio stays out of the repository)
listening_page.audio: mono mp3 96 kbps data URIs, each take gained to -21 LUFS integrated with a limiter at about -1.5 dBFS, so no voice wins by being louder

carolyn.library_description: Carolyn offers a warm, grounded American female voice with smooth resonance, clear natural articulation, and a calm, measured cadence. Her delivery is reassuring and conversational without sounding overly breathy, theatrical, or announcer-like.
carolyn.why_picked: Calm, measured cadence with clear articulation and warmth: the friendly end of an unhurried announcer, never cold.

samuel.library_description: A young British male voice with a calm, clear and quietly confident tone. Measured pacing and crisp diction keep long scripts easy to follow without ever sounding robotic. Ideal for documentaries, history and explainer videos, narration and audiobooks
samuel.why_picked: Measured pacing and crisp diction, explicitly 'without ever sounding robotic'; a British male to differ from the others.

ava.voice_name: Ava - Female Robot or AI Assistant
ava.library_description: Female voice over for AI assistant, GPS, virtual helper, robot character, etc.!
ava.why_picked: The 'system voice' end of the range (assistant, GPS): tests how machine-like the lift's own voice may be before it feels cold.

benjamin.library_description: A mature American male narrator with a calm, confident presence, clear diction, and a warm, steady low-mid tone. He delivers e-learning, corporate training, explainers, documentaries, and long-form narration at a measured, easy-to-follow pace. Professional and credible without sounding overly dramatic or announcer-heavy.
benjamin.why_picked: Calm, clear, measured and warm in a lower register: a mature American male counterpart to Carolyn.

sheldon.library_description: A nerdy, intelligent young male voice with an unmistakable youthful tone. Bright, expressive, and slightly awkward, with occasional natural voice cracks that add character and authenticity. Quick-witted, curious, and funny, with an infectious enthusiasm that comes through when excited. Equally suited to conversational storytelling, animated characters, cartoons, children's adventure audiobooks, and comedic voice acting.
sheldon.why_picked: Clever, quick-witted, curious and a little awkward: a capable, quirky friend; youthful without being a baby voice.

zibby.library_description: Zibby is a quirky, nerdy female character voice with lovable dorky energy, playful humor, and tons of personality. Awkward, animated, and expressive, she's perfect for animation, video games, NPCs, audiobooks, podcasts, and comedic narration. Ideal for nerdy best friends, awkward sidekicks, lovable weirdos, and quirky heroines.
zibby.why_picked: A nerdy best-friend sidekick with comic timing; the female option for the same 'fellow engineer' brief.

wilf.library_description: Perfect for comic storytelling, animation, storybooks, and games. Brings warmth, charm, and genuine character to every performance.
wilf.why_picked: Warmth and charm with a regional character; the grown-up, workshop-mate reading of Lifty, differing by accent and age.

kai.library_description: Bright, mid-high young male with tons of energy and personality. Perfect for anime-style protagonists and main leads. He can be goofy and nerdy one moment, then loud, proud and fully determined the next. Great for animation, video game heroes, quirky sidekicks, fan dubs and fun character content.
kai.why_picked: Bright, goofy-nerdy quirky sidekick: the high-energy end of the range. Replaced the first pick (Dexter Glitch), which the estimate priced at 2.25 times the normal rate.

sigma.library_description: Sigma Centauri is a calm, futuristic AI system voice with a classic space-computer tone. Ideal for spaceship announcements, onboard computers, sci-fi interfaces, robotic or android style characters, and narrative AI roles.
sigma.why_picked: The robot-by-voice end of the range, with no effects: a check on how much machine the owner wants in Lifty.

dan.library_description: Down-to-earth, warm baritone with a natural, conversational read that sounds like a real person, not an announcer. Made for social media and creator content: social media, Reels, faceless channels, fun facts and top-ten lists, explainers and tutorials, recipes, product reviews, storytime and podcasts.
dan.why_picked: Down-to-earth and real, not an announcer: a practical, friendly adult on the radio.

kiara.library_description: Warm, expressive African American female voice, medium-low pitch, smooth natural texture, relaxed conversational pacing, and subtle Southern-influenced warmth. Intelligent, witty, approachable, and quietly confident. Clear articulation with authentic rhythm, natural pauses, and expressive intonation. Never robotic or overly rehearsed.
kiara.why_picked: Intelligent, approachable, quietly confident with clear articulation: a crew lead who sounds capable and kind.

jamie.library_description: Male, British/English, warm and natural, moderately deep, conversational, confident, clear and relaxed. Slightly understated rather than 'announcer-like', with good natural variation in pitch.
jamie.why_picked: Confident, clear, relaxed and understated: the British option for a practical engineer.
